messages:
maria-g: Anyone else seeing weird queueing in us-west? GPUs appear idle in some nodes but new jobs stay PENDING for minutes.
ajay: Yep. Hit it ~10:15. Lots of short jobs piled behind a few long-running pods pinned to the same nodes. Admission controller isn't preempting.
k8s-bot: ALERT: admission_queue_depth(us-west-2)=218, avg_wait=94s, affected_pools=3
leo: Scheduler logs show a lot of "offer rejected: headroom insufficient" and repeated requeueing for the same podset. Could be ordering bug: a heavy long-running pod is evaluated before smaller waiting pods -> head-of-line blocking.
sam: We also have a rate-limit on route tokens that ties to cluster capacity. If capacity metric is stale for an AZ, the limiter throttles admission even when other AZs have free GPUs.
ajay: quick check: kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | sed -n '1,60p'

NAME                                READY   STATUS    NODE                IP           RESTARTS
inference-model-ckpt-0              3/3     Running   gpu-node-usw-12     10.0.3.21    0
inference-model-ckpt-1              3/3     Running   gpu-node-usw-12     10.0.3.22    0
inference-model-long-xyz            4/4     Running   gpu-node-usw-12     10.0.3.23    0
inference-ephemeral-abc             0/1     Pending   <none>              <none>       0
inference-ephemeral-def             0/1     Pending   <none>              <none>       0
...
ajay: see how three heavy pods are pinned to gpu-node-usw-12 while many short requests are blocked.
maria-g: That explains the hotspots. Any recent scheduler changes deployed last night?
leo: Deployed a change to the fair-share/token-bucket refiller at 02:30. I think refill window logic ignores nodeGroupCapacity when calculating available tokens -> leads to false headroom=0 for some pools.
sam: Risk: if we preempt aggressively to unblock the queue we lose KV cache locality and latency spikes will spike upstream. Need careful rollback or targeted preempt.
ajay: short-term mitigation: 1) reduce max_concurrency for model 'long-xyz' to 2 2) add nodeSelector to spread replicas across nodes 3) bump admission_parallelism from 18->30 so scheduler can make progress faster.
maria-g: Can you push the two config changes (max_concurrency + admission_parallelism) as a canary to us-west staging then prod?
ajay: I'll roll a canary in 5m. Patching rollout: /deploy configmaps/scheduler-config --patch '{"admission_parallelism":30}' then apply model config change.
leo: I'll also revert the token-bucket refiller commit in staging and run the test harness for multi-az occupancy.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0454 created by ajay. Priority: P0. Short description: us-west admission queueing / head-of-line node hotspots.
sam: Note for postmortem: add a regression test for refill accounting with uneven node group capacity and add per-node-group limiter metrics.
maria-g: Thanks team. Keep updates here. If the canary doesn't drop queue depth within 4m, we'll run the emergency scale-up playbook.
ajay: Canary applied to us-west-staging at 1812345880. Monitoring.
leo: Staging refiller revert tests passing. Planning to promote to prod after canary verification.
ajay: Canary reduced PENDING count from 170 -> 22 in 120s, GPU utilization across nodes went from 92% on node12 to ~60% average. Looks promising.
maria-g: Nice. Let's close this thread when the prod rollout finishes and add follow-ups to backlog: 1) fix refill algorithm 2) per-AZ capacity-aware rate limiter 3) scheduler unit to avoid long-pod head-of-line ordering.
sam: I'll file the backlog items after the incident is closed.
